val: noticed a short but sharp write-amplification wave on us-west4-ephemeral-cohort7 at ~09:27 UTC. GPU attach started failing for warmup and batch pods; attach success dropped ~35% for ~5m.

priya: any iostat / kernel hints?

val: pasted sample from affected host: ```iostat -x 1 2
Device:       r/s    w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await  %util
nvme0n1      0.50  470.00   4.00 11880.00   51.0    8.9    19.6 0.1  19.5  99.9
```

matt: avgqu and util look maxed. timeline? was janitor running?

val: janitor controller shows a flurry of verify jobs accepted ~09:25 but scheduler returned intermittent 429s; when limit lifted many hosts started scrubs and a few concurrent snapshotters kicked too. ops-bot: "scheduler: rate-limit hit cohort=cohort7"

oliver: us-west4 spare-ssd margin is low due to a mid-week reclaim. we tightened scrub cadence last sprint to reduce wear; looks like we bumped into overlap risk under higher attach load. also saw a couple hosts with thermal fan spin-ups at the same time.

priya: quick mitigations: 1) apply scrub backoff for cohort7 2) lower janitor concurrency and add pool-level coalesce guard 3) bump gpu attach soft-timeout to avoid immediate fallback 4) suspend noncritical snapshots for 15m. prefer 1+2+3 now.

matt: agree. also add a temporary soft-attach policy to prefer local-ssd-compatible warm nodes instead of remote fallback when possible (cost vs churn tradeoff).

val: executing now: ops-bot: `scheduler set-backoff --cohort cohort7 --duration 900s` and `janitor set-concurrency --cohort cohort7 --concurrency 1` at 09:29 UTC. updating autoscaler: attach_timeout 30s -> 90s in canary for us-west4.

ops-bot: "actions accepted: backoff applied, janitor concurrency set, autoscaler attach timeout patched (canary)"

oliver: monitoring queries to watch: `sum(rate(nvme_io_time_seconds_total[1m])) by (cohort)`, `avg(nvme_avg_queue_size{cohort="cohort7"})`, and `increase(gpu_attach_failed_total[5m])`.

priya: early effect: avgqu down from ~9 -> ~2 in ~4m and attach failures dropped under 1% by 09:33. we'll hold backoff 20m and then reintroduce scrubs with stricter coalesce.

matt: cost note: fallback/remap churn during the 5m window estimated +$720. logging to incident-costs.

val: follow-ups: 1) add scheduler hysteresis so rate-limit resets don't cause mass start, 2) add scrub tagging so we can migrate only checks that fix checksum issues (avoid full-verify migration), 3) investigate thermal spikes and firmware parity on hosts that saw CRC counts. creating tickets now.

oliver: also consider a short-term prefetch/warmup tweak for coldstarts (extract to tmpfs then flush) to reduce fsyncs during attach windows. file as opt-in proposal for workloads that can tolerate a slightly longer warmup.

val: leaving cohort7 backoff for 20m. will post if anything reoccurs. :white_check_mark:
